question: Which Montgomery census tracts have the highest adult diabetes prevalence?

answer.sql:
WITH cdc AS (
  SELECT
    tractfips AS geoid,
    CAST(diabetes_crudeprev AS DOUBLE) AS adult_diabetes_prevalence_per_adult,
    CAST(totalpop18plus AS BIGINT) AS adult_population
  FROM session.fw_ad2e8f_m1_cdc
)
SELECT
  t.name,
  c.adult_diabetes_prevalence_per_adult,
  c.adult_population,
  t.geoid
FROM fw_pg.tracts t
LEFT JOIN cdc c ON t.geoid = c.geoid
ORDER BY c.adult_diabetes_prevalence_per_adult DESC NULLS LAST, t.name ASC
LIMIT 200

reasons: The SQL correctly ranks Montgomery census tracts by CDC PLACES adult diabetes prevalence percentage, filtered to Montgomery County, AL, and returns 71 tracts sorted descending.

points: The top 5 tracts by adult diabetes prevalence are Tract 24 (31.5%), Tract 6 (28.5%), Tract 7 (28.2%), Tract 12 (28.0%), and Tract 11 (27.6%).
Tracts 22.01 and 59.02 are tied at 26.3% prevalence, each with adult populations of 2,870 and 2,442 respectively.
The ranking is based on CDC PLACES model-based percentage rates per adult resident, covering all 71 Montgomery census tracts in the dataset.
Prevalence decreases from 31.5% in Tract 24 to 24.6% in Tract 3 across the top 12 tracts.
caveats: CDC PLACES rates are model-based estimates from survey data, not census-complete counts.
Tied values (Tracts 22.01 and 59.02 at 26.3%) share a rank; the order within the tie is not distinguished by the source.
The underlying data year is not specified in the source metadata; the 2025 release date refers to dataset publication, not the survey year.
Rates are rounded to one decimal place, so small differences may not be statistically meaningful.
